root_cause.text: The jumbo_frm() function in chain mode unconditionally subtracts bmax from nopaged_len (linear bytes only), but is invoked based on total skb length including fragments, causing an integer underflow when the linear portion is smaller than bmax.
root_cause.evidence: CVE description and commit message explain that when nopaged_len <= bmax but skb->len > bmax due to page fragments, the subtraction of unsigned integers wraps, producing a huge len value. The patch fixes this by clamping buf_len to min(nopaged_len, bmax) before computing len.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix jumbo frame transmit to use the minimum of buffer size and actual data length to avoid over-mapping DMA when data is smaller than the buffer.
intent_record.what: Added a new variable `buf_len` set to `min_t(unsigned int, nopaged_len, bmax)`, updated `len` calculation to subtract `buf_len` instead of `bmax`, and replaced `bmax` with `buf_len` in `dma_map_single`, `tx_skbuff_dma[entry].len`, and `stmmac_prepare_tx_desc` calls.
intent_record.how: When `nopaged_len` is smaller than `bmax`, the DMA mapping and descriptor now use the actual data length instead of the full buffer size, preventing over-mapping and potential data access beyond the SKB data.

bic_trace_step.reason: The stmmac_jumbo_frm function in chain_mode.c computes len = nopaged_len - bmax without checking if nopaged_len >= bmax. Since nopaged_len is unsigned, this can underflow when the linear portion is smaller than bmax, leading to integer wraparound and subsequent incorrect DMA operations.
